questions.question: How do you select and manipulate DOM elements efficiently?
questions.title: Dom Manipulation Basics
questions.direct_answer: Select with querySelector/querySelectorAll (CSS selectors — the modern API); getElementById is the fastest for by-id. Create: document.createElement + set properties; insert: append/prepend/before/after; remove: el.remove(). Efficient patterns: batch DOM writes (build in a fragment or a string, insert once — each insert can trigger reflow), delegate events on stable parents, and classList/replaceChildren for bulk updates. Avoid: innerHTML loops per item (parse + re-layout per iteration) and layout reads interleaved with writes.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[querySelector / getElementById] --> M[mutate: create, append, remove, classList]
    M --> B[batch: fragment build → ONE insert]
    B --> R[ONE reflow instead of N]
    U[untrusted content?] -->|yes| T[textContent — never innerHTML]
    LIVE[live HTMLCollection: reflects mutations] -.static.-> SN[NodeList snapshot]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
Why innerHTML still has a place (the honest nuance): for large, TRUSTED, static markup it's faster than building nodes (one parse vs N createElement calls) — the template-literal pattern: list.innerHTML = items.map(i => '
  • ' + escapeHtml(i.name) + '
    • ').join(''). The rule isn't 'never innerHTML' — it's 'never innerHTML with untrusted interpolation.' The escape/insertAdjacentHTML pair (position control: beforebegin/afterbegin/beforeend/afterend) covers most cases cleanly. The NodeList vs HTMLCollection distinction (the API trivia that matters): querySelectorAll returns a STATIC NodeList (a snapshot — mutations don't affect your loop); getElementsBy* returns a LIVE HTMLCollection (reflects the DOM as it changes — the source of infinite-loop bugs when you remove elements while iterating a live collection you're also indexing). Static + forEach is why the modern API is both safer and easier. The framework connection (the interview-level close): React/Vue exist because hand-managed DOM state synchronization at scale produces the exact bug class this question tests — 'the DOM says X, my JS state says Y.' Frameworks made the DOM derived from state (re-render + diff) and eliminated the bookkeeping. But the primitives remain the diagnosis layer: understanding nodes, fragments, layout invalidation, and delegation is what lets you debug framework output (the Profiler shows DOM commits; the render pipeline explains why a list of 10,000 rows janks — the reason virtualization exists).
